intro: Gmaj7 and Dmaj7 alternate beneath a melody that holds notes across the accompaniment; the repeated span leads to a different final cadence. The score is aligned automatically, with provisional timings not checked by ear.
question: What changes when the same melody reaches its second ending?

sections.label: Modal turn and first ending · bars 19–39

relations.label: The opening music returns
relations.basis: The piece makes two large statements with different endings. The 87.5 s offset agrees with the return near 88 s, and the matched excerpt covers the repeated body rather than certifying the altered close. CENS diagonal mean 0.939, sustained 53.5 s, fixed pitch-class shift 0 semitones and time offset 87.5 s (cache/form/satie-gymnopedie-1.txt, candidate 1; 0.5 s grid). These are matched excerpts, not complete section boundaries; timing has not been checked by ear.

cues.title: Bass, then seventh chord
cues.text: The bass sounds on beat one; the upper accompaniment enters on beat two and holds through beat three. G–B–D–F♯ gives way to D–F♯–A–C♯: Gmaj7 alternating with Dmaj7, not four notes struck together.
cues.evidence: Bars 1–4, occurrence 1: Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, bottom and middle parts. G and D dotted-minim basses alternate beneath B–D–F♯ and A–C♯–F♯ minims after crotchet rests. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The melody enters late
cues.text: After four bars of accompaniment, the melody enters on beat two with F♯–A. Its opening phrase settles on F♯, tied across bars 9–12: keep following that held note while the bass and chords continue to change.
cues.evidence: Bars 5–12, occurrence 1: Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, top part, starts with a beat’s space then F♯–A; the F♯ beginning bar 9 is tied through bar 12. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Outside the Conservatoire
cues.text: Satie left home for Montmartre in 1887 and wrote the Gymnopédies in 1888. Two periods at the Paris Conservatoire had ended without a qualification; cabaret work became part of his livelihood.
cues.evidence: Steven M. Whiting’s Satie biography documents the Conservatoire periods, the 1887 move and the 1888 Gymnopédies: https://www.encyclopedia.com/people/literature-and-arts/music-history-composers-and-performers-biographies/erik-satie

cues.title: A modal change of colour
cues.text: A low E in the melody lasts three bars while the harmony changes beneath it. The following phrase brings C♮ and F♮ alongside B♮: over the persistent D bass, the minor third and raised sixth give a Dorian colour rather than an ordinary D-minor scale.
cues.evidence: Bars 19–29, occurrence 1: Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly. The top part ties E through bars 19–21, has A–B–C in bar 22 and E–F–G in bar 27; bottom holds D in each bar from 23 to 29. F♮ and B♮ support the D-Dorian reading. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Remember the first ending
cues.text: The first ending moves from G down to F♯ in the melody and eventually closes on D major. Listen for that major third, F♯: the second ending will replace it with F♮.
cues.evidence: Bars 32–39, occurrence 1: Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, first alternative. The top part begins G–F♯ in bars 32–33 and ends with D–F♯–A over the bottom part’s D bass in bar 39. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The opening returns
cues.text: The opening G bass returns for the second traversal. The same Gmaj7/Dmaj7 alternation prepares the melody again; this repeat retraces bars 1–31 before taking a different ending.
cues.evidence: Bar 1, occurrence 2, then bars 1–31, occurrence 2: Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, repeat volta and alternatives. The G bass and following B–D–F♯ chord restart the opening. Timing aligned automatically; score.json records this performed repeat.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: One note across four bars
cues.text: The melody reaches its long F♯ again. The accompaniment reattacks beneath it, but the melody’s tie asks for one continuous note across four bars, not four fresh melodic beginnings.
cues.evidence: Bars 9–12, occurrence 2: Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, top part has four tied dotted minims on F♯ while middle and bottom repeat their attacks. The tie begins at the start of bar 9. Timing aligned automatically; pedal and key-release timing are not established.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Debussy adds an orchestra
cues.text: Debussy orchestrated the first and third Gymnopédies in 1896. The second was not part of his pair. This recording uses Satie’s original medium, solo piano.
cues.evidence: The Concise Oxford Dictionary of Music entry lists the 1888 piano Gymnopédies and Debussy’s 1896 orchestrations of Nos. 1 and 3: https://www.encyclopedia.com/people/literature-and-arts/music-history-composers-and-performers-biographies/erik-satie

cues.title: Harmony moves under E
cues.text: On the repeat, follow the held E rather than just the bass. E-minor and G-major notes give way to D–F–A beneath the same melody note: the change of harmony does not require a new melodic attack.
cues.evidence: Bars 19–21, occurrence 2: Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly. Top ties E; middle gives G–B, then B–D–G, then F–A–D, above bottom E, E, D. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Counterpoint at thirty-nine
cues.text: In 1905 Satie entered the Schola Cantorum, studying with Vincent d’Indy and Albert Roussel. He was thirty-nine and had written the Gymnopédies seventeen years earlier.
cues.evidence: The Concise Oxford Dictionary of Music entry gives Satie’s 1866 birth, the 1888 Gymnopédies and his 1905 entry to the Schola Cantorum as a pupil of d’Indy and Roussel: https://www.encyclopedia.com/people/literature-and-arts/music-history-composers-and-performers-biographies/erik-satie

cues.title: The ending takes another route
cues.text: The second ending starts on the same melodic G, but its next long note is F♮ rather than F♯. An E bass persists beneath the altered phrase, delaying the final arrival on D.
cues.evidence: Bars 40–45, occurrence 1: Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, second alternative. Top has G in bar 40 and F♮ in bar 41; bottom has E in each of these six bars. Compare bars 32–37, occurrence 1. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: D minor replaces D major
cues.text: The last chord contains D, F♮ and A. Its minor third changes the ending without changing the final bass note: compare this D minor with the D major that closed the first traversal.
cues.evidence: Bar 47, occurrence 1: Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, top ends D–F–A–D over bottom D–A–D. Bar 39, occurrence 1, instead has F♯ in the top chord. The final chord starts at the bar line. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

transitions.title: One E outlasts the change of mode
transitions.how: The alternating G and D basses give way to F♯ minor in bar 17, B minor in 18 and E minor in 19. The melody drops from F♯ to a low E and holds it through bars 19–21. Beneath that single note, the accompaniment moves from G–B to G–B–D, then F–A–D: E minor becomes E minor seventh, then D minor with the melody’s E as an added ninth. The bass-on-one, chord-on-two rhythm continues; the change comes from register and harmony, not a new tempo.
transitions.evidence: The bar-19 section boundary maps to 42.928 s in score.json; the analysis report has a novelty boundary at 0:42. Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, top/middle/bottom, bars 17–21: bass F♯–B–E–E–D, tied melodic E, and the stated accompaniment pitches. The span uses bar-17 and bar-22 times. Automatic alignment remains provisional; the chord names are editorial readings of the written notes.

transitions.title: A closed chord restarts the accompaniment
transitions.how: Bars 38–39 close with A minor seventh, A–C–E–G, moving to D major, D–F♯–A. The C is natural: this is not the usual A-major dominant with C♯. After that held D-major chord, the returning G bass restores Gmaj7 as B–D–F♯ enters on beat two. Dmaj7 follows in bar 2. The melody is absent for four bars, so the repeat first sounds like a return to the accompaniment alone; its F♯–A opening arrives only in bar 5.
transitions.evidence: The Opening repeated boundary is bar 1, occurrence 2, at 90.340 s. Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, first alternative bars 38–39 and top/middle/bottom bars 1–5 establish the chords, staggered attacks and melodic rests. The source compresses Satie’s written-out return into a volta; these are its compact bar numbers. The analysis has a boundary at 1:28 and a quieter 1:30–1:35 passage; the form relation independently supports the repeated body, not an identical ending. Timing remains provisional.

transitions.title: The bass stays; the third changes
transitions.how: The repeated bar 31 has D–F♯–A–C over D. Bar 40 moves to E minor and the melody rises to G, just as at the first ending’s bar 32. The routes separate in bar 41: F♮ replaces F♯, and D–F–A sounds over E instead of the earlier F♯-minor chord. E remains in the bass through bar 45 while the melody changes. Bars 46–47 retain the earlier A-minor-seventh-to-D bass motion, but the final D chord now contains F♮. The same destination in the bass closes in minor rather than major.
transitions.evidence: The Different final cadence boundary is compact-source bar 40 at 158.528 s; the analysis has boundaries at 2:38 and 2:42. Mutopia 37, gymnopedie_1.ly, top/middle/bottom: compare first alternative 32–39 with second alternative 40–47, reached after bar 31 occurrence 2. The E bass persists through 40–45; the final F♮ is written in bar 47, aligned at 176.817 s. The span includes that chord without asserting a key-release time. The form relation does not certify identical endings; alignment is provisional.

composer.background:
Satie was born in the Norman port of Honfleur to a French father and a Scottish mother. After his mother died in 1872, he lived with his paternal grandparents and received lessons from a local organist. He later joined his father in Paris and entered the Conservatoire in 1879. His periods of study ended without the normal professional qualifications. His mature music would expose elementary actions — a bass note, a repeated chord, a scale fragment.

By the late 1880s he was working in Montmartre, including at the Chat Noir cabaret. The three Sarabandes of 1887 and Gymnopédies of 1888 came from this period. The latter use a slow triple metre, low bass notes and chords on the second beat. Major sevenths remain part of the sonority instead of being immediately corrected into consonances. Their regular accompaniment continues beneath a melody whose phrase-endings often avoid the sort of cadence that would make the next phrase feel inevitable.
composer.epithet: A cabaret pianist who separated repetition from development, and musical seriousness from ceremonial behaviour.
